reviews.review:
There's so much to say about Mass Effect Andromeda, i wouldn't know where to even begin so i'll try to keep it short and summarized. I've rarely seen such a bland but yet interesting game.  First of all; no, it's not "[i]the worst game ever made[/i]," far from it. The worst Mass Effect though? I'd agree with that. 

I'd say it's more or less the usual M.E. formula in a generic open world game with a bunch of issues. It feels like a 2007 game desperately trying to be a trendy 2015 game. You may have guessed it: yes it's overly repetitive, yes there are many fedex quests. But one my biggest gripes is the AI (for both squadmates and enemies): sometimes it's behaving normally, and sometimes it's criminally malfunctioning. The result is infuriatingly annoying gunfights. For some reason, it happens more in a particular open map, and less in a few others. Speaking of fighting, there's hardly any tactical aspect. Team abilities can synergize with yours and create a "combo" but what's the point when you can't pause the game and give specific orders to your squadmates like before? Most of the time, the combat is more akin to mindless shooting.  

Another gripe would be the UX and UI, they're oddly subpar in such a "modern" rpg. I mean you can't compare the stuff you craft/buy with the one you already have in real time. 

But the biggest issue imo is... ME:A is an unfortunate series of missed opportunities. There's a good explanation behind all of this: it's a widely unfinished software despite the big amount of content in it. Sure the devs managed to polish it enough and fix the bugs to make it playable, but there's in-depth design work that they would absolutely not be able to do. Whatever i did, wherever i went, i couldn't help but think "[i]would have been great if they did this or that, it needed to have something more, etc...[/i]" You more or less do the same thing all the time, talk with NPCs, go there, kill that, interact with this, come back, done. Nothing crazy, nothing memorable in both the story and the gameplay. They really needed to go overboard and write/make more unique situations. 

So why in tarnation am i recommending  ME:A anyway? I gotta admit, i liked it, i couldn't drop it nor did i ever want to. It just left me wanting for more to be honest. 

I dig the exploration. I was bummed when ME2 removed the planet exploration from ME1 and replaced it with a boring minigame instead of improving it. Obviously, it's back in Andromeda, you get to extract ore in free roam. Unfortunately, it's not as exciting as it sounds, there are hardly any secrets to be found.

Another good thing they brought back from ME1 is a much more detailed skill tree and the loot, LOTS of loot. I really missed it. It's not handled in the best way but it's there. Gameplay wise, ME:A feels more RPG than its two predecessors. 

The Nomad (new vehicle, replaced the Mako, upgradable but no guns attached) is fun to drive. 

You get to use a "scanner" to analyze some npcs, plants, enemies to read some lore about them and earn research points (much needed for your R&D crafting). It was severely underutilized but i enjoyed it. It reminded me of the Metroid Prime trilogy. 

The art style is fantastic, there are various picturesque sceneries to be seen. High screenshot potential if you ask me. Protip: there's sadly no implemented photo mode, but i've read that you can use Nvidia Ansel instead if you have a Nvidia GPU. 

On the whole, it was surprisingly addictive. If you like Action-RPGs, scifi, and the Mass Effect series, give it a chance. It's not incredible, you might not enjoy it, but it's definitely worth a try during sales. 

For reference, i didn't play the multiplayer mode and wasn't interested to.  Not sure if it has a lot of active players.

I had a lot of fun playing this game. I have played all of the mass effect games and this one is my favorite. That said, I do understand why many long time fans don't like this entry in the series. Ryder is not the hero Shepard is and I see that the studio tried to tell the story of a beginner being thrown into a huge role so of course Ryder won't have that same confidence and strength but they could of done a better job making a more likable personality.

Even playing the most updated version of this game glitches and bugs were not uncommon. On one of the planets everytime I died it would take literally 10min each time on a loading screen until I was finally spawned back. Quite annoying. There was another time where I had to clear all the enemies to progress and the last enemy was nowhere to be found. For the most part though the game functioned fine.

But regardless of the cons to this game, I really enjoyed it. The combat system is especially fun! There are many ways to play this game and collecting minerals and materials to upgrade or craft a new gun and the variety of skills and abilities make player customization satisfying and rewarding.

The worlds are all unique and a joy to explore. Your crew is interesting to get to know and the whole premise of exploring our neighbouring galaxy is thrilling and executed well.

Overall this is a great game. If your someone who doesn't get stuck up on a few flaws, then i'm sure your have as much fun as I did playing it.

Let's start with a story, the story was ok, i thought it's gonna be meh story from bioware but fortunately well design.

And now dialogue, it seem like the voice actor came to the studio to only to do their job and want to go home as fast as possible, especially Cora, the tone is flat lack of emotion as if the voice actor take the job only for the money.

Lastly the gameplay, personally i prefer the trilogy gameplay, they remove squad control in this game and i don't like it, which remove tactical gameplay standpoint, but the combat in this game much more fluid than their predecessor especially jumpjet and evade that add fluidity in this game, because of this, the gameplay become fast paced high intense combat like looter shooter games.

If you're a fan of trilogy, don't expect this game is similar to the trilogy mass effect, it's so different, but would i still recommend this game? yeah if it's on deep discount, full price NAH.

6.8/10

The "I have no idea why they all hated it" feeling evaporates in 2 hours and you start understanding, and then you realize people who played at launch also had bugs to help with their experience. 

In short - if you can play mass effect 1 and drive mako for an hour, followed by solving a 5x5 sudoku puzzle you can then experience a very polished earth defense force for about 30 seconds, and hear marvel 2025 level of cringe dialogue for a minute or two. Rinse and repeat for *checks playtime* 22 HOURS?! I've wasted a day on this!?
